items.punct_fr: en tête de phrase, suivi d'une virgule ; réservé à l'écrit
items.ex: [[Furthermore]], the employee was never told that his performance was a concern.

items.punct_fr: en tête de phrase, suivi d'une virgule ; trop lourd à l'oral
items.ex: [[Moreover]], the clause is unlikely to be enforceable.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; 'in addition to' + nom ou -ing, sans virgule
items.ex: [[In addition]], the company will cover your relocation costs.

items.punct_fr: pas de virgule ; après 'be' ou l'auxiliaire, avant le verbe principal
items.ex: We [[also]] need to update the staff handbook.

items.punct_fr: en fin de phrase, sans virgule
items.ex: Could you copy in the payroll team [[as well]]?

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; forme pleine 'what is more' à l'écrit soigné
items.ex: [[What's more]], she had already been warned twice.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; introduit un argument qui clôt la discussion
items.ex: [[Besides]], the deadline for appealing has already passed.

items.punct_fr: à l'oral, après une virgule ou en tête de phrase ; à éviter dans un document
items.ex: He's the only one who knows the system, [[plus]] he gets on with everybody.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; souvent pour une accumulation de problèmes
items.ex: [[On top of that]], nobody had told her about the meeting.

pitfalls_fr: 'Moreover' et 'furthermore' ne sont pas l'équivalent courant de 'de plus' : un anglophone les réserve aux écrits formels. À l'oral et dans un e-mail, 'also', 'and' ou 'as well' suffisent le plus souvent.
'Also' se place au milieu de la phrase ('We also need...'), rarement en tête. 'In addition' (adverbe, + virgule) ne se construit pas comme 'in addition to' (+ nom ou -ing).
'Besides' n'est pas neutre : il ajoute un argument décisif, parfois un peu sec. 'As well as' est suivi d'un nom ou d'un -ing ('as well as drafting the letter'), jamais d'une base verbale.

exercises.prompt: (formal report) The role was never advertised internally. ___, no selection criteria were recorded.
exercises.explain_fr: Dans un rapport, 'furthermore' convient. 'Plus' est familier ; 'as well' et 'too' se placent en fin de phrase.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) We'd have to retrain the whole team, and ___ we'd lose two months.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'oral, 'on top of that' est naturel. 'Furthermore' et 'moreover' sonnent comme un texte lu ; 'in addition to' exige un nom.

exercises.prompt: (email to a colleague) I've attached the contract. I've ___ copied in Payroll.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Also' se place entre l'auxiliaire et le participe. 'As well' et 'too' iraient en fin de phrase.

exercises.prompt: (written advice) ___ her basic salary, she receives a car allowance.
exercises.explain_fr: Devant un nom, il faut la préposition 'in addition to'. 'In addition' et 'moreover' sont des adverbes de phrase suivis d'une virgule.

exercises.prompt: The policy is out of date. It contradicts the collective agreement. (formal, written)
exercises.answer: The policy is out of date; moreover, it contradicts the collective agreement.
accept: The policy is out of date. Moreover, it contradicts the collective agreement.
The policy is out of date; furthermore, it contradicts the collective agreement.
The policy is out of date. Furthermore, it contradicts the collective agreement.
The policy is out of date and, moreover, contradicts the collective agreement.
The policy is out of date. In addition, it contradicts the collective agreement.
The policy is out of date and it also contradicts the collective agreement.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'écrit formel : point-virgule + 'moreover' ou 'furthermore' + virgule. Jamais une simple virgule avant ces adverbes.

exercises.prompt: He's always late. He never answers his emails. (informal, spoken)
exercises.answer: He's always late, and on top of that he never answers his emails.
accept: He's always late. On top of that, he never answers his emails.
He's always late, plus he never answers his emails.
He's always late and he never answers his emails either.
He's always late, and he never answers his emails either.
He's always late. Plus, he never answers his emails.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'oral : 'on top of that' ou 'plus'. Après une négation, 'either' remplace 'too' / 'as well'.

items.punct_fr: en tête : suivi d'une virgule ; au milieu : entre deux virgules ; jamais après une simple virgule pour relier deux phrases
items.ex: The offer was generous. [[However]], she turned it down.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ; relie deux propositions dans la même phrase
items.ex: Managers are paid monthly, [[whereas]] agency staff are paid weekly.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; compare deux situations différentes
items.ex: [[By contrast]], the Lyon site has had no resignations this year.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; situation inverse ; écrit uniquement
items.ex: [[Conversely]], an employee who resigns is not entitled to severance pay.

items.punct_fr: variante britannique soutenue de 'while' ; inusitée aux États-Unis
items.ex: The employer must give reasons, [[whilst]] the employee may resign without explanation.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; l'autre aspect d'une même question
items.ex: [[On the other hand]], a longer notice period would give us time to recruit.

items.punct_fr: virgule avant 'while' quand il exprime l'opposition
items.ex: Some teams are back in the office full time, [[while]] others are still fully remote.

items.punct_fr: virgule avant 'but' entre deux propositions ; en tête de phrase à l'oral seulement
items.ex: He accepted the warning, [[but]] he refused to sign it.

items.punct_fr: en fin de phrase, après une virgule ; typique de l'oral
items.ex: It's a good package. The notice period is long, [[though]].

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; on se ravise à voix haute
items.ex: [[Then again]], she might prefer to stay part-time.

pitfalls_fr: 'On the other hand' présente l'autre face d'une question (les deux sont vraies). 'On the contrary' contredit ce qui vient d'être dit ('au contraire'). Ne pas les confondre.
'However' n'est pas une conjonction : 'The offer was good, however she refused' est fautif. Il faut un point ou un point-virgule avant, une virgule après.
Calques à éviter : 'in contrary', 'at the opposite', 'in the contrary'. Dites 'by contrast', 'conversely' ou, à l'oral, simplement 'but'.

exercises.prompt: (formal report) Managers receive a bonus based on team results, ___ other employees are assessed individually.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Whereas' relie deux propositions opposées dans la même phrase. 'However' exigerait un point ou un point-virgule.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) The offer is generous. I'm not sure she'll accept it, ___.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Though' en fin de phrase est la façon orale de dire 'cela dit'. Les trois autres ne se placent pas en fin de phrase.

exercises.prompt: (written advice) A resignation takes effect once notice is given. ___, a dismissal must follow a set procedure.
exercises.explain_fr: 'By contrast' compare deux situations. 'On the contrary' contredirait la phrase précédente ; 'whereas' ne commence pas une phrase indépendante.

exercises.prompt: (in conversation) 'So you think the claim will fail?' - '___, I think she has a strong case.'
exercises.explain_fr: On réfute ce que l'autre vient de dire : 'on the contrary' ('au contraire').

exercises.prompt: UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day. US employees have no statutory right to paid leave. (formal, written)
exercises.answer: UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day, whereas US employees have no statutory right to paid leave.
accept: UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day, while US employees have no statutory right to paid leave.
UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day, whilst US employees have no statutory right to paid leave.
UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day; by contrast, US employees have no statutory right to paid leave.
UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day. By contrast, US employees have no statutory right to paid leave.
UK employees accrue paid leave from their first day; however, US employees have no statutory right to paid leave.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Whereas' / 'while' (UK aussi 'whilst') dans une seule phrase, ou 'by contrast' après un point ou un point-virgule.

exercises.prompt: The salary is lower. The benefits are much better. (spoken)
exercises.answer: The salary is lower, but the benefits are much better.
accept: The salary is lower. The benefits are much better, though.
The salary is lower, though the benefits are much better.
The salary is lower. On the other hand, the benefits are much better.
The salary is lower; however, the benefits are much better.
The salary is lower. However, the benefits are much better.
The salary is lower but the benefits are much better.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'oral, 'but' ou 'though' en fin de phrase suffisent ; inutile de sortir 'however'.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; après un point ou un point-virgule
items.ex: The delay was short. [[Nevertheless]], it amounted to a breach of the procedure.

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule, ou en fin de phrase
items.ex: The evidence is thin; the allegation must [[nonetheless]] be investigated.

items.punct_fr: + nom, sans virgule entre les deux ; langue des contrats
items.ex: [[Notwithstanding]] clause 4, the Company may vary the place of work.

items.punct_fr: + adjectif, adverbe ou groupe nominal, jamais une proposition complète
items.ex: The parties reached an agreement, [[albeit]] a fragile one.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; virgule à la fin de la subordonnée placée en tête
items.ex: [[Although]] he apologised, the warning stays on his file.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; reprend la phrase précédente
items.ex: She has only been here a month. [[Even so]], she is entitled to a week's notice.

items.punct_fr: + nom ou -ing ; jamais 'despite of'
items.ex: [[Despite]] several reminders, the form was never returned.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; idéal en réunion comme à l'écrit courant
items.ex: [[That said]], I think we should still take legal advice.

items.punct_fr: en tête, suivi d'une virgule ; oral
items.ex: [[Still]], it's better than nothing.

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule ou en fin de phrase
items.ex: I know he's busy. I'd like a quick word with him [[all the same]].

pitfalls_fr: Pas de double marquage : 'Although he apologised, but...' est fautif. Choisissez 'although' OU 'but'.
'Despite' se construit directement ('despite the delay', 'despite being late'). 'Despite of' n'existe pas ; 'in spite of' prend 'of'.
'Even if' = hypothèse ('même si, à supposer que') ; 'even though' = fait réel ('bien que'). 'Even though she was warned' : elle a bien été avertie.

exercises.prompt: (formal letter) You apologised promptly. ___, the misconduct was serious enough to justify a final written warning.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Nevertheless' : registre soutenu, en tête de phrase. 'Still' est oral ; 'despite' veut un nom ; 'although' une subordonnée.

exercises.prompt: (written) ___ repeated reminders, he failed to return the equipment.
exercises.explain_fr: Devant un groupe nominal, seul 'despite' convient.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) I know it's expensive. ___, I think we should get proper legal advice.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'oral : 'still'. 'Notwithstanding' et 'albeit' appartiennent à l'écrit juridique.

exercises.prompt: (contract clause) ___ clause 4, the Company may require the Employee to work at other sites.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Notwithstanding' + nom : 'nonobstant'. C'est le connecteur de dérogation des contrats.

exercises.prompt: She had only been there two months. She was entitled to notice. (everyday)
exercises.answer: Although she had only been there two months, she was entitled to notice.
accept: Even though she had only been there two months, she was entitled to notice.
She was entitled to notice although she had only been there two months.
She was entitled to notice even though she had only been there two months.
She had only been there two months. Even so, she was entitled to notice.
She had only been there two months; nevertheless, she was entitled to notice.
She had only been there two months, but she was still entitled to notice.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Although' / 'even though' + proposition, ou 'even so' après un point. Jamais 'although... but'.

exercises.prompt: The procedure was followed. It was followed slowly. (formal - use 'albeit')
exercises.answer: The procedure was followed, albeit slowly.
accept: The procedure was followed, albeit slowly
The procedure was followed, albeit rather slowly.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Albeit' + adverbe ou adjectif : concession très concise, réservée à l'écrit.

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule, ou en fin de proposition
items.ex: [[To some extent]], the dispute could have been avoided.

items.punct_fr: souvent entre virgules ; 'on peut soutenir que'
items.ex: The restriction is, [[arguably]], wider than the business needs.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule
items.ex: [[Strictly speaking]], a freelancer is not covered by the staff handbook.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; s'oppose à 'in principle' / 'in theory'
items.ex: [[In practice]], nobody takes the full lunch break.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; 'dans l'ensemble'
items.ex: [[On the whole]], the consultation went smoothly.

items.punct_fr: souvent après 'I agree' ; sous-entend un désaccord poli
items.ex: I agree with you [[up to a point]].

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; 'en règle générale'
items.ex: [[As a rule]], we don't give references over the phone.

items.punct_fr: avant l'adjectif ou le participe, ou seul en réponse
items.ex: The handbook is [[more or less]] ready.

items.punct_fr: avant le verbe ou l'adjectif ; familier
items.ex: We've [[pretty much]] agreed on the figures.

items.punct_fr: avant l'adjectif ou le verbe ; UK aussi 'sort of' ; jamais à l'écrit
items.ex: It's [[kind of]] awkward to raise it now.

pitfalls_fr: 'In fact' et 'indeed' ne sont pas des tics de liaison. 'In fact' corrige ou renforce ('en réalité') ; 'indeed' confirme ou insiste. Pour 'en effet' explicatif, on ne met souvent rien, ou 'because'.
'Normally' au sens de 'normalement, il devrait...' se dit plutôt 'in principle' ou 'should' : 'She should be back on Monday'.
'Globally' signifie 'dans le monde entier'. Pour 'globalement', dites 'on the whole', 'overall' ou 'broadly'.

exercises.prompt: (written advice) The restriction is, ___, wider than is necessary to protect the business.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Arguably' : nuance d'expert à l'écrit. 'Globally' = 'mondialement' ; les deux autres sont familiers.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) ___, yes, she can work from home, but in practice her manager wants her in on Mondays.
exercises.explain_fr: 'In principle... but in practice' : le couple naturel. 'Normally speaking' n'existe pas.

exercises.prompt: (chatting with a colleague) The handbook is ___ finished - I just need to check the leave section.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Pretty much' = 'quasiment', registre familier.

exercises.prompt: (formal email) ___, a consultant is not an employee, although the two are often treated alike day to day.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Strictly speaking' : 'à strictement parler', pour rappeler la règle avant de nuancer.

exercises.prompt: The new policy has worked. Absence is still high in one team. (use 'on the whole')
exercises.answer: On the whole, the new policy has worked, although absence is still high in one team.
accept: On the whole, the new policy has worked, but absence is still high in one team.
On the whole the new policy has worked, although absence is still high in one team.
The new policy has worked on the whole, although absence is still high in one team.
The new policy has worked on the whole, but absence is still high in one team.
On the whole, the new policy has worked, though absence is still high in one team.
exercises.explain_fr: 'On the whole' annonce un bilan globalement positif avant la réserve.

exercises.prompt: I agree with you. I don't think we should dismiss him. (use 'up to a point')
exercises.answer: I agree with you up to a point, but I don't think we should dismiss him.
accept: I agree with you up to a point but I don't think we should dismiss him.
Up to a point I agree with you, but I don't think we should dismiss him.
I agree with you up to a point. I don't think we should dismiss him, though.
exercises.explain_fr: 'I agree up to a point' : formule de désaccord poli, très utilisée en réunion.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; virgule après le groupe placé en tête
items.ex: [[Owing to]] a restructuring, the role will move to Dublin.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; écrit soutenu
items.ex: He was excused from night shifts [[on account of]] his health.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; 'compte tenu de'
items.ex: [[In view of]] her length of service, a longer notice period is appropriate.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; 'given' + nom
items.ex: [[Given that]] the deadline has passed, the appeal cannot be heard.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; pas de virgule avant en général
items.ex: We can't sign today [[because]] the client hasn't approved the figures.

items.punct_fr: + nom
items.ex: The hearing was postponed [[because of]] the rail strike.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; cause déjà connue de l'interlocuteur
items.ex: [[Since]] you were not informed, we will extend the deadline.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; très courant dans les avis et les e-mails
items.ex: The office is closed today [[due to]] maintenance work.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; oral, plus fréquent au Royaume-Uni
items.ex: [[Seeing as]] you're here, could you look at this letter?

items.punct_fr: + nom(s) ; énumère des causes, oral
items.ex: [[What with]] the audit and the pay review, we haven't had a minute.

pitfalls_fr: 'Because' + proposition, 'because of' + nom. 'Because of he was late' est fautif.
'Due to the fact that' est un tic administratif : dites 'because'. De même, 'thanks to' ne s'emploie que pour une cause favorable.
'As' causal est ambigu (cause ou temps) ; préférez 'because' ou 'since' quand la cause est l'information importante.

exercises.prompt: (formal letter) The hearing has been postponed ___ the unavailability of your representative.
exercises.explain_fr: Devant un nom, registre soutenu : 'owing to'. 'Because', 'since' et 'seeing as' exigent une proposition.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) We can't sign today ___ the client hasn't approved the figures.
exercises.explain_fr: Devant une proposition (sujet + verbe), seul 'because' convient.

exercises.prompt: (chatting) ___ you're already here, could you have a quick look at this letter?
exercises.explain_fr: 'Seeing as' + proposition : 'vu que', familier.

exercises.prompt: (written advice) ___ the employee's length of service, a longer notice period would be appropriate.
exercises.explain_fr: 'In view of' + nom : 'compte tenu de'. 'Given that' serait suivi d'une proposition.

exercises.prompt: The meeting was cancelled. There was a rail strike. (everyday)
exercises.answer: The meeting was cancelled because of a rail strike.
accept: The meeting was cancelled because there was a rail strike.
The meeting was cancelled due to a rail strike.
The meeting was cancelled owing to a rail strike.
The meeting was cancelled as there was a rail strike.
The meeting was cancelled since there was a rail strike.
The meeting was canceled because of a rail strike.
The meeting was cancelled because of the rail strike.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Because of' + nom est la solution la plus légère.

exercises.prompt: He has a long disciplinary record. A final warning is justified. (formal, written)
exercises.answer: Given his long disciplinary record, a final warning is justified.
accept: In view of his long disciplinary record, a final warning is justified.
Given that he has a long disciplinary record, a final warning is justified.
A final warning is justified given his long disciplinary record.
A final warning is justified in view of his long disciplinary record.
Since he has a long disciplinary record, a final warning is justified.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Given' / 'in view of' + nom condensent la cause en tête de phrase.

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule, ou entre le sujet et le verbe sans virgule
items.ex: The notice was sent to the wrong address and was [[therefore]] invalid.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; fréquent dans les lettres et décisions
items.ex: [[Accordingly]], your appeal has been dismissed.

items.punct_fr: + nom, sans verbe ; écrit uniquement
items.ex: The role has disappeared; [[hence]] the need for a consultation.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; lourd à l'oral
items.ex: [[Consequently]], the bonus will not be paid this year.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; 'as a result of' + nom
items.ex: [[As a result]], two members of the team have resigned.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ; reprend toute la proposition
items.ex: She's on leave until the 15th, [[which means]] we can't meet before then.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule
items.ex: [[For that reason]], we recommend putting the change in writing.

items.punct_fr: virgule avant 'so' ; en tête de phrase à l'oral seulement
items.ex: He didn't reply, [[so]] I called him.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; oral et e-mails courants
items.ex: [[That's why]] we need her signature before Friday.

pitfalls_fr: 'Thus' ne traduit pas le 'ainsi' de liaison français : il est rare et très soutenu. À l'écrit préférez 'therefore', à l'oral 'so'.
'Hence' se construit avec un nom ('hence the delay'), pas avec une proposition complète dans l'usage courant.
Commencer une phrase par 'So,' est normal en réunion mais déplacé dans un avis écrit ; 'consequently' ou 'accordingly' prononcés en réunion font l'effet inverse.

exercises.prompt: (formal letter) You failed to attend two hearings without explanation. ___, the decision was taken in your absence.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Accordingly' : 'en conséquence', ton d'une lettre officielle. 'So that' exprime le but.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) She's on leave until the 15th, ___ we can't hold the interview before then.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'oral, après une virgule : 'so'. Les autres sont des adverbes écrits et ne relient pas deux propositions après une virgule.

exercises.prompt: (written) The role no longer exists; ___ the need for a redundancy consultation.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Hence' + groupe nominal, sans verbe : 'd'où'.

exercises.prompt: (chatting) Nobody told him about the deadline. ___ he's annoyed.
exercises.explain_fr: 'That's why' + proposition : 'c'est pour ça que'.

exercises.prompt: The notice was sent to the wrong address. It was not validly served. (formal, written)
exercises.answer: The notice was sent to the wrong address and was therefore not validly served.
accept: The notice was sent to the wrong address; therefore, it was not validly served.
The notice was sent to the wrong address. Therefore, it was not validly served.
The notice was sent to the wrong address; consequently, it was not validly served.
The notice was sent to the wrong address. Consequently, it was not validly served.
The notice was sent to the wrong address. As a result, it was not validly served.
The notice was sent to the wrong address; accordingly, it was not validly served.
The notice was sent to the wrong address and therefore was not validly served.
exercises.explain_fr: 'And was therefore...' : 'therefore' au milieu, sans virgules, est la tournure la plus élégante.

exercises.prompt: The budget was cut. We had to freeze recruitment. (spoken)
exercises.answer: The budget was cut, so we had to freeze recruitment.
accept: The budget was cut. That's why we had to freeze recruitment.
The budget was cut, which is why we had to freeze recruitment.
The budget was cut, which meant we had to freeze recruitment.
The budget was cut. As a result, we had to freeze recruitment.
The budget was cut so we had to freeze recruitment.
exercises.explain_fr: À l'oral : 'so' ou 'that's why'.

items.punct_fr: + base verbale ; négatif : 'in order not to'
items.ex: The policy was amended [[in order to]] reflect the new legislation.

items.punct_fr: + base verbale ; surtout au négatif : 'so as not to'
items.ex: The rota was redrawn [[so as to]] give every team one free weekend in two.

items.punct_fr: + -ing (ici 'to' est une préposition)
items.ex: We are consulting staff [[with a view to]] introducing flexible hours.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; formule de définition dans les contrats
items.ex: [[For the purposes of]] this clause, 'Group' includes all subsidiaries.

items.punct_fr: + base verbale ; la solution par défaut
items.ex: I'm writing [[to]] confirm the arrangements for your first day.

items.punct_fr: + sujet + can / will / could ; pas de virgule avant
items.ex: I'll send the draft tonight [[so that]] you can read it before the call.

items.punct_fr: + base verbale ; présente un objectif
items.ex: [[The aim is to]] reduce turnover by the end of the year.

items.punct_fr: 'so that' sans 'that' ; oral
items.ex: Send it to me today [[so]] I can check it before the meeting.

items.punct_fr: + base verbale ; oral, présente un projet sans solennité
items.ex: [[The idea is to]] get everybody in the same room for once.

pitfalls_fr: Jamais 'for' + infinitif : 'I'm writing for to confirm' et 'for confirm' sont fautifs. Le but d'une action se dit 'to' + verbe. ('For' + -ing décrit l'usage d'un objet : 'a form for claiming expenses'.)
'In order to' alourdit la phrase quand 'to' suffit. Gardez-le pour lever une ambiguïté ou dans un texte formel.
Au négatif : 'so as not to' / 'in order not to', et non 'to not' ou 'for not'. 'With a view to' est suivi de -ing.

exercises.prompt: (written) The company has introduced exit interviews ___ identifying the causes of staff turnover.
exercises.explain_fr: Devant un -ing, seul 'with a view to' est possible : 'to' y est une préposition.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) I'll send you the draft tonight ___ you can read it before the call.
exercises.explain_fr: Sujet différent + 'can' : 'so that'.

exercises.prompt: (email) I'm writing ___ confirm the arrangements for your first day.
exercises.explain_fr: But = 'to' + base verbale. 'For to' est un calque de 'pour'.

exercises.prompt: (formal) The names have been removed ___ breach confidentiality.
exercises.explain_fr: But négatif : 'so as not to' (ou 'in order not to', avec 'to').

exercises.prompt: We are reviewing the pay structure. We want to close the gender pay gap. (everyday)
exercises.answer: We are reviewing the pay structure to close the gender pay gap.
accept: We are reviewing the pay structure in order to close the gender pay gap.
We are reviewing the pay structure so as to close the gender pay gap.
We are reviewing the pay structure with a view to closing the gender pay gap.
We are reviewing the pay structure so that we can close the gender pay gap.
We're reviewing the pay structure to close the gender pay gap.
exercises.explain_fr: Même sujet dans les deux phrases : 'to' + verbe suffit.

exercises.prompt: She recorded the meeting. Nobody could dispute what was said. (everyday)
exercises.answer: She recorded the meeting so that nobody could dispute what was said.

She recorded the meeting so that no one could dispute what was said.
She recorded the meeting so no one could dispute what was said.
exercises.explain_fr: Sujets différents : 'so that' + sujet + 'could' (au passé).

items.punct_fr: + présent ; 'that' peut tomber ; pas de 'will'
items.ex: Leave may be carried over [[provided that]] the line manager agrees in writing.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; 'in the event of' + nom

items.punct_fr: inversion : 'should' + sujet + base verbale ; remplace 'if'
items.ex: [[Should]] you need any adjustments for the interview, please let us know.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; 'sous réserve de'
items.ex: [[Subject to]] satisfactory references, we would like to offer you the post.

items.punct_fr: virgule après la subordonnée placée en tête ; jamais 'will' après 'if'
items.ex: [[If]] she accepts, we can start on the first of the month.

items.punct_fr: = 'if... not' ; verbe à la forme affirmative
items.ex: We'll go ahead on Thursday [[unless]] we hear otherwise.

items.punct_fr: + présent ; condition suffisante, ton courant
items.ex: You can swap shifts [[as long as]] your manager knows.

items.punct_fr: après un point ou un point-virgule, suivi d'une virgule ; 'sinon'
items.ex: Please reply by Friday. [[Otherwise]], we will assume you are not interested.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ; oral ; peut sonner comme une menace

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; ouvre une hypothèse à l'oral
items.ex: [[Supposing]] he says no, what do we do then?

pitfalls_fr: Pas de 'will' ni de 'would' après 'if', 'unless', 'provided that', 'as long as' : 'if he accepts', jamais 'if he will accept'.
'In case' ne veut pas dire 'si' : il exprime une précaution ('Take a copy in case they ask for it'). 'Au cas où vous seriez malade' = 'If you are ill'.
'Unless' contient déjà la négation : 'unless you don't object' dit le contraire de ce que vous voulez. Calque à éviter : 'at the condition that' (dites 'on condition that' ou 'provided that').

exercises.prompt: (contract) The Employee may work remotely ___ the Line Manager has given prior written approval.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Provided that' : 'à condition que', registre contractuel.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) You can carry the days over ___ you take them before March.
exercises.explain_fr: 'As long as' : la version courante de 'provided that'.

exercises.prompt: (policy) ___ the Employee be unable to attend, the hearing will be rescheduled once.
exercises.explain_fr: La base verbale 'be' révèle l'inversion formelle : 'Should the Employee be unable...'.

exercises.prompt: (email) We'll go ahead on Thursday ___ we hear otherwise from the union.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Unless' = 'sauf si'. Avec 'otherwise', 'if' donnerait le sens inverse.

exercises.prompt: You don't give a month's notice. You will lose the bonus. (use 'unless')
exercises.answer: Unless you give a month's notice, you will lose the bonus.
accept: You will lose the bonus unless you give a month's notice.
Unless you give a month's notice, you'll lose the bonus.
You'll lose the bonus unless you give a month's notice.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Unless' + verbe affirmatif au présent ; 'will' seulement dans la principale.

exercises.prompt: The parties fail to agree. The matter will be referred to mediation. (formal, written)
exercises.answer: In the event that the parties fail to agree, the matter will be referred to mediation.
accept: Should the parties fail to agree, the matter will be referred to mediation.
If the parties fail to agree, the matter will be referred to mediation.

exercises.explain_fr: 'In the event that' ou l'inversion 'Should the parties fail...' : deux marques de l'écrit juridique.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; écrit
items.ex: [[By way of example]], a manager may not ask a candidate about her family plans.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ; moins fréquent que 'notamment' en français
items.ex: Several benefits are taxable, [[notably]] the company car.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ; introduit la liste complète, pas un exemple
items.ex: Two documents are missing, [[namely]] the signed contract and the job description.

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule, ou après une virgule
items.ex: The audit raised several concerns, [[in particular]] the lack of written contracts.

items.punct_fr: entre virgules ; en tête, suivi d'une virgule
items.ex: You could, [[for example]], offer her a phased return to work.

items.punct_fr: même ponctuation que 'for example'
items.ex: [[For instance]], we could move the weekly meeting to the afternoon.

items.punct_fr: + nom(s) ; virgule avant si l'exemple est accessoire
items.ex: Serious offences [[such as]] theft or fraud may lead to summary dismissal.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ; jamais en tête de phrase comme connecteur
items.ex: Morale is low, [[especially]] in the night-shift team.

items.punct_fr: + nom ; à l'écrit soigné, préférer 'such as'
items.ex: We should offer perks [[like]] gym membership or extra leave.

items.punct_fr: entre virgules ; propose un exemple chiffré ou une hypothèse
items.ex: Could we meet next week - [[say]], Tuesday morning?

pitfalls_fr: 'Comme' introduisant un exemple se dit 'such as' ou 'like', pas 'as' : 'benefits such as a company car'. Et 'like for example' est redondant.
'e.g.' = 'for example' ; 'i.e.' = 'that is' (c'est-à-dire). Ils ne sont pas interchangeables et ne se prononcent pas en réunion.
'Namely' annonce tous les éléments ('à savoir'), pas un échantillon. 'Notamment' se rend plus naturellement par 'in particular' ou 'including' que par 'notably'.

exercises.prompt: (formal policy) Gross misconduct includes serious offences, ___ theft, violence and fraud.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Such as' + noms. 'As' seul ne signifie pas 'comme par exemple' ; 'like for example' est redondant.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) We could offer something extra - ___, two more days' leave.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Say' : façon orale d'avancer un exemple ou un chiffre.

exercises.prompt: (written) Only one member of the panel dissented, ___ the HR Director.
exercises.explain_fr: On nomme précisément la personne : 'namely' ('à savoir'), pas un exemple parmi d'autres.

exercises.prompt: (written advice) Several benefits are taxable, ___ the company car.
exercises.explain_fr: 'In particular' : 'notamment'. 'Say' est oral ; 'as' ne convient pas.

exercises.prompt: Some costs can be reclaimed. Travel and accommodation can be reclaimed. (everyday)
exercises.answer: Some costs, such as travel and accommodation, can be reclaimed.
accept: Some costs can be reclaimed, such as travel and accommodation.
Some costs, for example travel and accommodation, can be reclaimed.
Some costs can be reclaimed, for example travel and accommodation.
Some costs, for instance travel and accommodation, can be reclaimed.
Some costs can be reclaimed, for instance travel and accommodation.
Some costs, like travel and accommodation, can be reclaimed.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Such as' + exemples, entre virgules parce que l'information est accessoire.

exercises.prompt: Two documents are missing. They are the signed contract and the job description. (use 'namely')
exercises.answer: Two documents are missing, namely the signed contract and the job description.
accept: Two documents are missing: namely, the signed contract and the job description.
Two documents are missing, namely the signed contract and the job description
exercises.explain_fr: 'Namely' énumère la totalité de ce qui vient d'être annoncé.

items.punct_fr: entre virgules ; écrit ; lourd à l'oral
items.ex: The contract is open-ended, [[that is to say]], it has no fixed end date.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule
items.ex: [[To put it another way]], the burden of proof lies with the employer.

items.punct_fr: écrit uniquement ; précédé d'une virgule ou entre parenthèses
items.ex: Fixed-term employees, [[i.e.]] those whose contracts have an end date, are also covered.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; affine ce qui précède
items.ex: He left in March or, [[more precisely]], on the last working day of March.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; valable à l'écrit comme à l'oral
items.ex: [[In other words]], the clause cannot be enforced.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; annonce une version sans jargon
items.ex: [[Put simply]], we are paying two people to do the same job.

items.punct_fr: précédé d'une virgule ou d'un tiret ; on se corrige
items.ex: We need to talk to her manager, [[or rather]] her former manager.

items.punct_fr: + proposition ; pour clarifier en réunion
items.ex: [[What I mean is]] we shouldn't promise anything in writing yet.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; résume sans détour ; à ne pas répéter à chaque phrase
items.ex: [[Basically]], he wants more money and fewer hours.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; reformulation spontanée
items.ex: It's not ideal. [[I mean]], it works, but nobody likes it.

pitfalls_fr: 'C'est-à-dire' ne se traduit pas mécaniquement par 'that is to say' : à l'oral dites 'I mean', 'in other words' ou 'which means'.
'Concretely' est un calque de 'concrètement' : dites 'in practice', 'in practical terms' ou 'specifically'. De même, 'en clair' = 'put simply', pas 'clearly'.
'i.e.' reformule, 'e.g.' donne un exemple. Si la liste n'est pas complète, c'est 'e.g.'.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) The role is being 'restructured' - ___, it's being made redundant.
exercises.explain_fr: 'In other words' passe aussi bien à l'oral qu'à l'écrit. 'i.e.' ne se dit pas ; 'that is to say that' est un calque.

exercises.prompt: (written) Employees on fixed-term contracts, ___ those whose contracts have a set end date, are also covered.
exercises.explain_fr: On définit le terme, on ne donne pas un exemple : 'i.e.'.

exercises.prompt: (chatting) ___, he wants more money and fewer hours.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Basically' : résumé direct, registre familier.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) We'll need to speak to her manager - ___, her former manager.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Or rather' : on se corrige ('ou plutôt').

exercises.prompt: The clause is void. It has no legal effect. (use 'in other words')
exercises.answer: The clause is void; in other words, it has no legal effect.
accept: The clause is void. In other words, it has no legal effect.
The clause is void - in other words, it has no legal effect.
The clause is void, in other words it has no legal effect.
The clause is void: in other words, it has no legal effect.
exercises.explain_fr: 'In other words' après un point ou un point-virgule, suivi d'une virgule.

exercises.prompt: He was not dismissed. He resigned before the hearing. (formal - use 'more precisely' or 'rather')
exercises.answer: He was not dismissed; more precisely, he resigned before the hearing.
accept: He was not dismissed. More precisely, he resigned before the hearing.
He was not dismissed; rather, he resigned before the hearing.
He was not dismissed. Rather, he resigned before the hearing.
He was not dismissed - rather, he resigned before the hearing.

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule ou en fin de phrase ; surtout britannique
items.ex: Concerns should be raised with your line manager [[in the first instance]].

items.punct_fr: en tête avec virgule, ou avant le verbe
items.ex: She was suspended and [[subsequently]] dismissed.

items.punct_fr: souvent en fin de proposition ; langue des contrats
items.ex: Salary is reviewed after six months and annually [[thereafter]].

items.punct_fr: + nom ou -ing ; 'before' suffit presque toujours
items.ex: References will be taken up [[prior to]] any offer of employment.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; 'firstly' possible à l'écrit, jamais 'at first'
items.ex: [[First]], we need to establish the facts.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; 'after' seul n'est pas un adverbe
items.ex: [[After that]], HR will write to confirm the outcome.

items.punct_fr: + proposition au présent ou au present perfect ; pas de 'will'
items.ex: [[Once]] the investigation is complete, you will be invited to a hearing.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; dernier point d'une liste
items.ex: [[Finally]], please remember to return your security pass.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; oral, d'origine américaine mais compris partout
items.ex: [[First off]], thanks for coming at such short notice.

items.punct_fr: suivi d'une virgule ; oral
items.ex: [[To start with]], let's go through last month's figures.

pitfalls_fr: 'At first' = 'au début' (et la suite a changé). Pour énumérer, dites 'first' ou 'first of all'. 'In a first time' n'existe pas.
'Eventually' = 'finalement, au bout du compte', jamais 'éventuellement' (= 'possibly'). 'At last' exprime le soulagement ('enfin !'), pas le dernier point d'une liste ('finally', 'lastly').
'After' seul ne peut pas commencer une phrase comme adverbe : dites 'after that', 'afterwards' ou 'then'.

exercises.prompt: (formal procedure) The complaint is investigated by HR. ___, a written report is sent to both parties.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Subsequently' : 'par la suite', écrit formel. 'After' seul est impossible ; 'eventually' = 'au bout du compte'.

exercises.prompt: (in a meeting) ___, thanks for coming at such short notice.
exercises.explain_fr: 'First off' ouvre une réunion sur un ton détendu. 'At first' = 'au début'.

exercises.prompt: (written) ___ the investigation is complete, you will be invited to a hearing.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Once' + présent : 'une fois que'. Les autres sont des adverbes, pas des conjonctions.

exercises.prompt: (contract) The first review will take place after six months and annually ___.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Annually thereafter' : collocation contractuelle ('puis chaque année').

exercises.prompt: You must inform your manager. Then you may book the leave. (use 'before' or 'prior to' + -ing)
exercises.answer: You must inform your manager before booking the leave.
accept: You must inform your manager prior to booking the leave.
You must inform your manager before you book the leave.
Before booking the leave, you must inform your manager.
Prior to booking the leave, you must inform your manager.
Before you book the leave, you must inform your manager.
exercises.explain_fr: 'Before' / 'prior to' + -ing quand le sujet est le même.

exercises.prompt: She completed her probation. She was given a permanent contract. (use 'once')
exercises.answer: Once she had completed her probation, she was given a permanent contract.
accept: Once she completed her probation, she was given a permanent contract.
She was given a permanent contract once she had completed her probation.
She was given a permanent contract once she completed her probation.
